## zarf_package_pull

Fetch a zarf package to disk.

Write it as `colonel_byte.zarf.zarf_package_pull`. It runs zarf on the node the task is delegated to; nothing is installed on the cluster's nodes.

Added in `colonel_byte.zarf` 0.88.0.

Runs `zarf package pull` to fetch a package from an `oci://` registry or an `https://` URL and write it to a directory as a tarball.

The module is a compiled binary with zarf linked into it. It renders the `zarf package pull` command line from these parameters, executes zarf's own command in its own process, and reports one JSON result. It needs no `zarf` on the node.

It is the staging half of an air-gapped workflow: a connected node fetches the package, something carries the file through the airlock, and `colonel_byte.zarf.zarf_package_deploy` reads it from the path it landed at. Nothing it does reaches a cluster.

### Parameters

| Parameter                  | Type   | Required | Flag                         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `package`                  | `str`  | yes      | None                         | The package to fetch: an `oci://` reference or an `https://` URL. The positional argument of the command, so it renders no flag.                                                                                      |
| `output_directory`         | `str`  | no       | `--output-directory`         | The directory the tarball is written to. Zarf defaults it to the working directory, which under Ansible is whichever directory the module was invoked from, so a playbook that cares where the package lands says so. |
| `shasum`                   | `str`  | no       | `--shasum`                   | The SHA256 checksum of the package. Zarf requires it for a package fetched over `https://` rather than merely accepting it.                                                                                           |
| `zarf_config`              | `str`  | no       | None                         | A zarf config file, passed as `ZARF_CONFIG`. It is how a playbook keeps registry credentials out of the argument vector.                                                                                              |
| `wrapper_binary`           | `str`  | no       | None                         | The module wrapper to run, resolved on the path when it holds no separator. The action plugin consumes this parameter; the wrapper never sees it.                                                                     |
| `parameters`               | `dict` | no       | None                         | Further module parameters, merged into the ones given directly. A parameter given both directly and inside `parameters` is an error naming it. The action plugin consumes this key; the wrapper never sees it.        |
| `oci_concurrency`          | `int`  | no       | `--oci-concurrency`          | How many OCI operations zarf runs at once.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `architecture`             | `str`  | no       | `--architecture`             | The architecture of the package to fetch, for a reference that publishes more than one.                                                                                                                               |
| `cache`                    | `str`  | no       | `--cache`                    | Zarf's cache directory.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `tmpdir`                   | `str`  | no       | `--tmpdir`                   | The directory zarf unpacks into while it works.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `plain_http`               | `bool` | no       | `--plain-http`               | Whether zarf talks to OCI registries over plain HTTP.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `insecure_skip_tls_verify` | `bool` | no       | `--insecure-skip-tls-verify` | Whether zarf skips verifying TLS certificates it connects to.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `log_level`                | `str`  | no       | `--log-level`                | Zarf's log level.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `log_format`               | `str`  | no       | `--log-format`               | Zarf's log format. Defaults to `json`.                                                                                                                                                                                |

### Notes

- Set `run_once: true` and `delegate_to` on the task. The package is fetched once, to the node holding the staging directory.
- `changed` is an observation here rather than a convention: the task reports changed only when the pull left a package file the output directory did not already hold, with `zarf.changedSignal` set to `complete` and the filenames in `zarf.packagesPulled`. Zarf derives the filename from the package's own metadata, so that list is how a playbook learns what to deploy.
- Check mode reports the task as skipped. `zarf package pull` has no dry run.
- A `package` that is a local path is refused: there is nothing to fetch. Use the path directly with `colonel_byte.zarf.zarf_package_deploy`.
- A parameter left unset renders no flag, so whatever zarf's own config file sets still applies.

### Example

```yaml
- name: Stage a package for the airlock
  colonel_byte.zarf.zarf_package_pull:
    package: oci://ghcr.io/colonel-byte/zarf/csi-local-path-provider:0.0.37-upstream
    output_directory: /srv/staging
  delegate_to: localhost
  run_once: true
  register: pull_result

- name: Deploy what was staged
  colonel_byte.zarf.zarf_package_deploy:
    package: "/srv/staging/{{ pull_result.zarf.packagesPulled | first }}"
    kubeconfig: /etc/rancher/rke2/rke2.yaml
  delegate_to: localhost
  run_once: true
  when: pull_result.zarf.packagesPulled | length > 0
```
